newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Blast kills one near Sri Lankan leader's holiday home.
newsitem.headline: Blast kills one near Sri Lankan leader's holiday home.

text.p: An explosion near the official holiday home of Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga killed one person on Monday, police said.
They said the blast occurred about 250 metres (yards) from the entrance of the house at 2.30 p.m. (0830 GMT) in the central hill country town of Nuwara Eliya.
Kumaratunga, who was in Nuwara Eliya for an election meeting, was not in the house at the time of the explosion and was unharmed, they said.

"We have arrested one man," a police official told Reuters by telephone from Nuwara Eliya, the colonial-style hill country resort and capital of the country's tea industry 65 miles (105 km) east of Colombo.
Details on the person killed were not immediately available.
Officials at the house said Kumaratunga was at the election meeting being held at municipal grounds in the town.
Witnesses said police had cordoned off the area. The cause of the blast was not immediately clear, police said.
Kumaratunga is addressing a series of election meetings across the country ahead of local government polls scheduled for March 21.
Police have said they fear increased violence ahead of the polls and warned political parties of possible attacks at election rallies.

The Centre for Monitoring Election Violence said at the weekend that nearly 500 incidents of election-related violence, mostly threats against candidates and their supporters, had been reported up to Friday.
The election has already been marred by the February killing of a ruling coalition legislator in southern Sri Lanka.
